title: Who Took Ensley's Color Away?
intro: Welcome, rainbow explorer! Read Ensley's story. Answer reading and math questions to earn Lit Bucks. You get two tries. If an answer is tricky, use the hint and try again. Mistakes help your rainbow grow!

pages.text: School was over, and Ensley wanted to play. The African grasslands looked sunny and fun.
But Ensley had two hours of homework to do. “Two hours?” Ensley groaned. “That feels longer than Grandpa’s old wrinkly neck!”
“Ensley took a deep breath and got started.” She put her books, pencils, and papers on the table.
Then she lost her pencil. It was behind her ear.
Ensley saw five mango slices on her plate. Her mom gave her three more. “Five plus three equals eight!” cheered Ensley. 5 + 3 = 8
Then Ensley tried another problem. She was sure she was correct.
Her tummy felt tight. “I worked so hard! How can I be wrong?” She protested.
WHOOSH! A tiny red spark flew off Ensley’s side. Ensley looked at her spots. Her red spot was gone!
Next, Ensley practiced reading. She came to a word she did not know.
She tried once, then tried once more. At last she read the word correctly.
ZIP! A blue spark raced around the room. “My blue spot too?” cried Ensley. “Someone is stealing my rainbow!”
“Next, Ensley played a memory game.” She had to remember four shapes.
A colorful butterfly flew past her nose. “And just like that, Ensley forgot every single one.”
Ensley took a breath and tried again. This time she remembered all four shapes. A green spark popped from her side. “HA!” said Ensley. “I knew it!”
Ensley made a clue board. She drew sparks, books, numbers, and question marks.
“My colors vanish when I study,” she whispered. “The Rainbow Thief must be near!”
Then Ensley got three answers wrong in a row. Her papers were everywhere.
Outside, the other animals ran and played. “I don’t want to do one more thing,” Ensley said.
A tiny yellow spark floated past her nose. Then a soft voice sang, “Wrong is not the end!” “Look once more, my colorful friend. Fix one thing, and follow the light!”
“Ensley did not try to finish everything at once.” She picked just one problem.
There were nine birds in a tree, and four flew away. “Nine minus four is five!” said Ensley. 9 − 4 = 5
Suddenly, every spark appeared at once. They flew out the door and across the grass.
Ensley searched for her backpack. “My backpack is missing!”
Ensley chased the sparks past rocks and tall grass. “Wait for me!” she shouted.
The trail led toward the oldest acacia tree. That was strange, because Ensley knew that tree.
Three zebras stood by the tree. Two more zebras walked over.
“Three plus two is five,” said Ensley. The tree began to glow. 3 + 2 = 5
Ensley peeked into the glowing hollow. All of her missing colors were inside!
Red, yellow, green, and blue spun in the air. Orange, indigo, and violet joined them too.
Something sat underneath the glowing colors. “Ensley gasped in surprise.”
It was her turquoise school backpack! She had left it under the tree two days ago.
The rainbow sparks showed Ensley what had happened. One spark appeared each time she learned something hard.

“They appeared when she got something wrong.” They appeared when she tried again. They appeared when she remembered. They appeared when she focused. They appeared when she solved a problem. They appeared when she fixed a mistake.
The colors had not been stolen at all. They had been growing brighter.
WHOOSH! The seven colors rushed back to Ensley. Her rainbow shone brighter than ever.
Homework was still hard sometimes. Ensley still wished she had more time to play.
But now she knew something important. A wrong answer did not mean she could not learn.
“I solved the mystery!” Ensley cheered. “Now I am ready to go home!”
Then she stopped. “Where is my pencil?” “Her friends laughed. ‘Ensley! It’s behind your ear again!’”

questions.prompt: What was under the glowing colors?

questions.prompt: Were the colors really stolen?

questions.prompt: How did Ensley change by the end?

questions.prompt: Which idea best fits the rainbow colors?

questions.explanation: The colors can represent learning and growth. Tell your grown-up another idea the story supports.

questions.prompt: What helped her keep going?

questions.prompt: What funny thing happened again at the end?

questions.explanation: One change made the task feel manageable and helped her move forward.
